item.title: ‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record
item.description:
The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?

Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.

It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association.

item.dc:creator: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor

item.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
item.description:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Associated Press

item.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
item.description:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg

item.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
item.description:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg

item.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
item.description:
Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

item.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
item.description:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent

item.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
item.description:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Leyland Cecco in Toronto

item.title: Colombia’s president arrives at scene of supermarket hostage siege in tourist city
item.description:
Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Tiago Rogero, South America correspondent, and agencies

item.title: Kilmar Ábrego García, man at center of Trump deportation battle, leaves US
item.description:
Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain

Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain.

A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his final destination.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Cris Seda Chabrier in New York

item.title: Canada says it ‘does not report to the US’ after Pentagon criticizes military spending
item.description:
Scathing US document memo supposedly ‘atrophied’ defence capabilities of its northern neighbour

Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour.

The document, released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Leyland Cecco in Toronto

item.title: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern
item.description:
Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election

The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.

Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Eva Corlett in Wellington

item.title: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections
item.description:
Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party

Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.

Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years, are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Amy Hawkins and Yu-chen Li in Taipei

item.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
item.description:
Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’

  • Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.

Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bailey and agencies

item.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
item.description:
Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far east

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Justin McCurry in Tokyo

item.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
item.description:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bailey and agencies

item.title: Heatwaves, floods, fires and rain: weekend of weather extremes expected across Australia
item.description:
As bushfires ravage Flinders Island, Victorians can expect a wet and windy election day as storms forecast on east coast

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Major fires are among a multitude of weather extremes forecast across Australia on Friday and into the weekend, which also includes severe storms, heavy rain, floods and heatwaves.

Firefighters contending with an out-of-control bushfire on Flinders Island expected conditions to deteriorate further on Friday, as authorities confirmed at least eight buildings had been destroyed or significantly damaged.

item.title: Qantas and Air New Zealand planes too close at Sydney airport as ‘mental models’ of crews to be investigated
item.description:
Aborted descent on Wednesday morning is latest in a series of landing incidents at Sydney airport

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating flight crews’ “mental models” after a Qantas plane aborted its landing at Sydney airport on Wednesday after noticing another aircraft crossing the runway while on its descent.

The ATSB said Qantas flight 426 from Melbourne was due to land just before 10.15am on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 jet told to expect a late landing clearance due to aircraft crossing the runway.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Nick Visser

item.title: Coalition teams up with Labor to pass 20% gas reservation scheme for Australia’s largest exporters
item.description:
Labor passes final major piece of legislation for 2026, denying Greens’ bid for 25% tax on exports

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A federal gas reservation scheme requiring Australia’s largest exporters to keep up to 20% of their product for domestic use will go ahead with the Coalition’s support.

The opposition waved through the government’s plans in the in a late night Senate sitting on Thursday night, giving Labor the numbers it needed. A short sitting of the lower house rubber stamped changes, seeing the legislation pass parliament.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

item.dc:creator: Tess Ikonomou

item.title: Sam Wood to spend Christmas in jail after again being denied bail over alleged assault of wife Snezana
item.description:
Former Bachelor star and fitness influencer stands accused of assaulting wife at Noosa in Queensland during family holiday in October

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Reality star Sam Wood will spend Christmas in jail after again being denied bail on domestic violence charges over allegations he strangled and assaulted his wife while the family was holidaying at Noosa on the Sunshine Coast in October.

The court of appeal today heard a third application by Wood, 46, for bail. He has spent eight weeks in custody since being arrested.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Joe Hinchliffe

item.title: Southern and central Australia face summer of heightened bushfire risk and heatwaves
item.description:
Fire chiefs say large swathes of the country are at risk from fires driven by high fuel loads, dry soil and hot weather

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Large parts of southern and central Australia face elevated fire risk this summer, authorities say, while heatwaves and extreme temperatures are likely nationwide.

Most of Victoria, eastern Tasmania and large parts of South Australia, Western Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory face heightened bushfire risk – driven by high fuel loads, low soil moisture and forecast hot and dry conditions – according to the seasonal outlook from the Australian and New Zealand Council for Fire and Emergency Services (AFAC), released on Friday.

Continue reading...

item.title: How much of the sharp fall in UK immigration is due to Labour’s policies?
item.description:
Labour is jubilant it has got numbers down to levels the Tories could not but it was helped by factors beyond its control

  • Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic

David Cameron was the leader of the opposition when he made a comment on overall migration that was used to interrogate every Tory leader for the next 14 years.

Asked in January 2010 on the BBC by the interviewer Andrew Marr to address comments made by the archbishop of Canterbury calling for the population to remain under 70 million, Cameron said net immigration levels of 200,000 a year were “too much”.

item.dc:creator: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor

item.title: What would happen if Russia detonated a nuclear weapon in space?
item.description:
⁠Sputnik-S, a nuclear-enabled satellite, has been assembled by Russia and could be launched in 60 days, reports say

Russia is reportedly preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite into space later this year, in a scenario that could pose a significant threat to global communications.

German media outlets have reported, citing western intelligence agency assessments, that such a satellite could be launched within 60 days and would be operational shortly afterwards.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Dan Milmo and Aisha Down

item.title: EU leaders wrestle over Ukraine aid as potential Le Pen victory sparks fear
item.description:
Slovakia, Hungary and Czechia want to opt out of €45bn Ukraine loan, as Germany tries to protect funding from possible far-right French presidency

  • Europe live – latest updates

EU leaders were bracing for a clash over long-term financial aid for Ukraine amid an effort to finalise high-stakes budget talks by the end of the year.

Arriving in Brussels on Thursday, the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, reiterated his view that all EU member states should support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine for 2027. “When the European Union provides funding, it does so as the European Union – and that union consists of 27 member states, not 23 or 24,” he said.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels

item.title: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos wins race to be next ECB president
item.description:
Former Bank of Spain governor chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde after winning support of EU’s biggest countries

Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen as the next president of the European Central Bank, to succeed Christine Lagarde, after winning support from the EU’s biggest countries.

The economist and monetary policymaker will become the first Spaniard to lead the ECB, defeating his rival candidate Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels

item.title: Labour’s EU reset deal will be ‘floor not ceiling’, says Burnham cabinet ally
item.description:
Scottish secretary Douglas Alexander to say Britain cannot secure the change it needs ‘without changing our relationship with Europe’

Labour’s EU reset deal will be a “floor not a ceiling”, according to a close cabinet ally of Andy Burnham, who says the UK has been a “cork bobbing on the tides of history” because of the power lost by Brexit.

Douglas Alexander, the Scottish secretary, will tell a conference in Italy on Friday that the government cannot deliver the major change Britain needs “without changing our relationship with Europe. When the status quo is not working, you don’t stand still. You move forward. When the status quo is broken, you don’t ignore it. You fix it.”

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jessica Elgot, Lisa O’Carroll and Jennifer Rankin

item.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says
item.description:
Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza City

Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter.

On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”

item.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
item.description:
Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decade

Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).

This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Emma Graham-Harrison and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem

item.title: UN sacked Palestinian staff on back of unproven Israeli allegations, tribunal rules
item.description:
Judgment casts doubt on evidence linking aid workers to Hamas and says humanitarian efforts in Gaza were damaged

A UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.

The judgment, seen by the Guardian, raises fresh questions about the decision by the UN Relief and Works Agency (Unrwa), the main humanitarian organisation working in Gaza, to sack members of staff. It was taken on the basis of Israeli allegations of involvement in the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Julian Borger Senior international correspondent

item.title: Palestinian journalist killed by Israel in Gaza wins Rory Peck prize
item.description:
Mariam Dagga shares award with two of her colleagues from AP for ‘powerful coverage’ of human cost of war

Mariam Dagga, the Palestinian war correspondent who was killed at the age of 33 in Gaza in an Israeli strike, has posthumously won the prestigious Rory Peck prize for freelance video journalists, the organisers announced on Wednesday.

She shares the award with two of her colleagues from the Associated Press (AP), Abdel Kareem Hana and Jehad Alshrafi, “for their powerful coverage of the human cost of the war” in the Palestinian territory, the Rory Peck Trust said.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Nadeem Badshah

item.title: Pro-Palestine activist sought by US in extradition case: ‘I still have a right to my beliefs’
item.description:
James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, at center of legal fight, says he ‘should not be unjustly accused’ because of leftwing views

James “Fergie” Chambers, the wealthy leftwing activist and donor controversially sought in extradition by the US, has told the Guardian that he is “not asking anyone to endorse my ideas or not think I’m a jerk – but I still have a right to my beliefs and should not be unjustly accused because of them”.

Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Timothy Pratt

item.title: Oxford museum displays seized belongings of Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu for first time
item.description:
Notebooks, clothes and ritual objects taken by British forces in India in the 1930s go on show at Pitt Rivers Museum

In 1932, British forces in north-east India imprisoned a 17-year-old girl called Gaidinliu for leading an uprising against colonial rule. While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions.

They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: David Batty

item.title: Politician hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
item.description:
Six helipads built and feast prepared by 500 cooks for wedding hosted by Anant Singh, an MP charged with murder

It takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024. Estimates of the cost for the months-long celebration ran to at least $600m, with world leaders and celebrities among those on the guest list.

Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi

item.title: Indian Cockroach movement leader asks court for permission to fly to UK
item.description:
Officials at Delhi airport stopped Saurav Das from boarding flight to Britain, where students have invited him to speak

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has asked the Delhi high court to give him permission to fly to the UK after immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him boarding a flight early on Tuesday morning.

The court is scheduled to hear Saurav Das’s case on Thursday morning. His lawyer asked the court for a quick hearing because Das has by now already missed some of his engagements at British universities and can only attend the other events on his itinerary if he is allowed to fly out as soon as possible.

item.title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov play to 38-move draw – as it happened
item.description:
• Sindarov and Gukesh play to 38-move draw in Game 1

  • Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered

  • Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’

  • Play through 22 famous world championship games

The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess.

The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable weapons against 1 e4.

item.dc:creator: Bryan Armen Graham

item.title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
item.description:
Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May. Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse in Delhi

item.title: Water firms to identify 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts
item.description:
Department for Work and Pensions to provide data about households missing out on WaterSure support scheme

Water companies will use government data to identify as many as 250,000 vulnerable households in England eligible for discounts, after criticism that not enough people are aware of the £428 support for their annual bills.

The Department for Work and Pensions will provide information to identify and contact a quarter of a million households who are missing out on support to which they are entitled under the WaterSure scheme.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jasper Jolly

item.title: Nearly half of ethnic minority people in UK have faced racism at work in last year, survey finds
item.description:
Figures show impact on mental health, with majority having no confidence HR will take their concerns seriously

Nearly half of people from minority ethnic backgrounds have experienced racism at work and the majority have no confidence that HR would take their concerns seriously, a survey has found.

It also found that 75% of people from the UK’s five largest minority ethnic communities had experienced racism or unfair treatment linked to their race, ethnicity or religion in the previous year, and three-quarters of those who had experienced racism said it had affected their mental health to some degree.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Tobi Thomas

item.title: Chance of snow forecast for northern England and Scotland in next few days
item.description:
Met Office warns of icy roads and risk of freezing rain on higher ground as weather turns cold and unsettled

Parts of England could see snow in the coming days as cold and unsettled weather continues into the weekend, forecasters have said.

Heavy rain sweeping eastwards on Friday could turn to snow over higher ground in northern England and Scotland.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Nadeem Badshah

item.title: Net migration to UK falls to lowest level since 1997 excluding pandemic
item.description:
Latest figures show difference between number of people arriving and leaving UK was ⁠77,000 in ​year ‌to ‌June

  • Analysis: How much of the fall in UK immigration is due to Labour’s policies?

Net migration across the UK has fallen to its lowest level since 1997 with the exclusion of the years of the Covid pandemic.

Figures released by the Office for National Statistics and the Home Office show that the difference between people arriving and leaving the UK was ⁠77,000 in ⁠the ​year ‌to ‌June ‌2026.

item.dc:creator: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor

item.title: Nottingham man jailed for 12 years for drugging and sexually assaulting partner
item.description:
‘Depraved’ predator attacked victim while she was under the influence of sleeping tablets he had given her

A man has been jailed for 12 years for drugging his long-term partner and sexually assaulting her while she slept.

The man, who is in his 30s and from Nottingham, cannot be named in order to protect the identity of his victim. At a hearing in June, he admitted sexually assaulting the woman on multiple occasions while she was under the influence of sleeping pills.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent

item.title: Strobe Talbott, Time magazine reporter and deputy US secretary of state, dies aged 80
item.description:
After 21 years at Time, Talbott joined the Clinton administration and later headed the Brookings Institution

Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.

His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he died peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press

item.title: Trump alleges ‘fake’ economic figures released before US midterms but doesn’t provide evidence
item.description:
In a Thanksgiving post, the US president seeks investigation after blue wave of Democrats unseat Republicans

Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party.

In a holiday message on social media tinged with bitterness, the US president wished a happy thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Edward Helmore

item.title: US Senate ‘permitting bill’ threatens clean water protections to speed up energy projects
item.description:
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act passed the Senate and is now being debated in the House

An industry-backed “permitting bill” approved by the US Senate would gut key clean water protections with changes that would do little to speed up the development of major energy projects, advocates warn.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (Baaja) passed the Senate 62-33 and is now being debated in the House. The Baaja is a “permitting reform” bill that aims to reduce the time it takes federal agencies to approve major energy and infrastructure projects, like power lines, fossil fuel pipelines, natural gas plants and datacenters.

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Tom Perkins

item.title: Fifa confirms cyber-attack exposed ‘personal and business information’
item.description:
Football’s governing body says hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business data

Fifa confirmed that hackers gained access to a “limited set of personal and business information” in a cyber-attack, amid heightened concern over digital vulnerabilities of leading organizations and institutions.

The global soccer governing body said it “condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data”, in a statement to the Associated Press on Thursday. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”

Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Keely Aouga and agencies

item.title: US army calls detonation of bomb chemicals in Iowa a success after fears of toxic plume
item.description:
The army blows up US stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used for explosives, to avoid uncontrollable explosion

The US army blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, saying the first checks show Wednesday’s controlled detonation in Iowa didn’t spread toxic dust to nearby homes and farms.

Earthen barriers were put up and foam and water were poured onto a pair of bunkers holding the 5 tons (4,500kg) of lead azide, and officials said those measures appear to have absorbed much of the blast.
